Right: the returned graph keeps every cycle edge and adds two fill edges in the accent color, 2 to 5 and 3 to 5, cutting the cycle into three triangles. Filled badges give the elimination numbering alpha: node 1 is 5, node 2 is 4, node 5 is 3, node 3 is 2, and node 4 is 1." width="100%"} Every graph can be made chordal by adding *fill* edges. This method adds an inclusion- minimal set of them (no fill edge can be dropped while staying chordal), which keeps the triangulation close to the original graph. Triangulating is the first step of building a junction tree for exact inference in Bayesian and Markov networks, of ordering sparse Cholesky factorizations, and of computing tree decompositions. Parallel edges count once and self-loops are ignored when searching; the original edges are all kept. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[Graph, dict[int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph with every node and edge of this one plus the fill edges, and the elimination numbering `alpha` (node ID to a position from `n` down to `1`, in the order the nodes were visited). Eliminating nodes in increasing `alpha` adds no further edges. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} MCS-M (Berry, Blair, Heggernes and Peyton, 2004) visits nodes by largest weight; when node `z` is visited, every unvisited `y` that can be reached from `z` through unvisited nodes of smaller weight than `y` gets its weight increased, and becomes a fill neighbor of `z` if not already adjacent. Here the reachability test is one bottleneck search per visited node, $O(V E \log V)$ overall. The fill edges and the numbering match NetworkX's `complete_to_chordal_graph` (which returns all-zero numbers for an already chordal graph; EdgeCase always returns the ordering). ## Examples {.doc-examples} A 5-cycle needs two chords to become chordal: ::: {#e02284f7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ring = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(5) chordal, alpha = ring.complete_to_chordal_graph() chordal.count_edges() - ring.count_edges(), chordal.is_chordal() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (2, True) ``` ::: :::
